blockIp.title: Block an IP
blockIp.help: Block an IP from SSH right away, without waiting for failed logins. It stays blocked until you unblock it.

whitelist.title: Whitelist
whitelist.help: These IPs are never blocked, whatever they do. Use it for your office IP or monitoring servers.

pages.whitelistDesc: IPs fail2ban never blocks, however many logins fail.
pages.blocklistDesc: IPs blocked from SSH. Block a new one, or unblock one fail2ban caught.
pages.sshDesc: Recent SSH logins and failed attempts. Block an IP that keeps trying, or unblock one fail2ban caught.

policy.title: SSH login protection
policy.help: An IP that fails to log in to SSH this many times within a day is blocked. Bans from every jail never expire on their own; they last until you unblock the IP here. The panel stays reachable, so you can always unblock yourself.
policy.temporary: Temporary block (not managed by dPanel yet)
policy.tempJails: These jails still unban on their own: {jails}. Click Save to make their bans permanent.

shell.notInstalled: fail2ban is not installed on this server. Install it with {cmd}.
shell.notRunning: fail2ban is installed but not running, so nothing is blocked. Start it with {cmd}.

banned.title: Blocked IPs
banned.jailStats: {banned} blocked · {failed} failing now · {total} blocked in total
banned.empty: No IPs are blocked right now.

history.title: SSH login history
history.latest: The latest {count} SSH logins from the system journal, newest first.

actions.loadHistoryFailed: Could not load SSH login history.
actions.banConfirmSelf: Block {ip} from SSH permanently? This is your own IP: you will lose SSH access until you unblock it here.
actions.bulkBanConfirmSelf: Block {count} from SSH permanently? Your own IP is in the selection: you will lose SSH access until you unblock it.
actions.bulkWhitelistConfirm: Whitelist {count}? fail2ban will never block them, and any current block is lifted.
actions.deleteHistoryConfirm: Delete the login history of {count}? Blocks and the whitelist stay as they are, and new attempts from these IPs still show.
actions.clearHistoryConfirm: Clear the whole SSH login history? Blocks and the whitelist stay as they are; only logins after now will show.
actions.whitelistRemoveConfirm: Remove {ip} from the whitelist? It can be blocked again after failed logins.

geo.private: Private or local network address, so it has no place on the map.
geo.pending: Not located yet. It fills in once the DB-IP database is downloaded.
geo.unknown: The DB-IP database has no place for this address.
geo.located: Located from the local DB-IP database (city-level, not exact).

detail.far: {distance}. Far from the IP's city: VPN, proxy or a faked position?
detail.notShared: Not shared (only required when the panel is opened over HTTPS)

map.title: Where logins come from
map.legend: Green: successful logins, red: failed attempts, amber: both. Bigger circles mean more events. A white ring marks a device (GPS / Wi-Fi) location; the rest are IP locations.
map.notDownloaded: The IP location database is not downloaded yet, so logins are saved without a place. Download it once (about 130 MB); it then updates itself every month and fills in the saved rows.

location.httpsNote: Every common browser gives a location here once the user allows it.
location.httpNote: Most browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge) give no location over plain HTTP, except on localhost or with a setting that trusts the site.
location.whyHttp: Most browsers give no location over plain HTTP, so most people will not be able to log in over HTTP.
location.whyHttps: A browser that blocks location, or a device without location services, will not be able to log in.
location.intro: The login form can ask the browser for the device's GPS / Wi-Fi position, far more exact than the IP's city. Set a rule for each protocol. Test on your own browser before you make it required.
location.youAreOn: You are on {scheme} now; the test runs here.
location.notTestedHttp: Not tested on {scheme}; most browsers give no location over HTTP. If browsers give nothing, nobody can log in over {scheme}.
location.notTested: Not tested on {scheme}. If browsers give nothing, nobody can log in over {scheme}.
location.lockedOut: Locked out? On the server, in the panel folder, run {cmd} (both protocols; add {flag} for one).

panel.shellHelp: Blocking login sets the shell to nologin: SSH (password or key) and su stop working. The user's websites and cron jobs keep running.
panel.rootNote: root always keeps a login shell so the server stays recoverable.
panel.lockHelp: Locking disables password login only; SSH keys still work while the shell allows login.

rules.title: Detection Rules
rules.subtitle: {count} of {total} rules enabled. Disabled rules are skipped when scan results are saved.
rules.uploadHelp: Checks every file uploaded through File Manager, Website Import, cPanel import and App Installer with ClamAV before it is saved. PHP files are also checked for webshells and obfuscated code. Infected files are rejected.
rules.uploadRam: Runs the ClamAV daemon, which keeps about 1–1.5 GB of RAM in use while this is on. Turning it on takes up to a minute while signatures load.
rules.blocked: ClamAV is not running, so every upload is being refused. Turn scanning off to let uploads through.
